mission: Orthogonal is a small agent-foundations alignment group founded in 2023 by Tamsin Leake. It pursues 'formal-goal alignment': writing down, mathematically, a goal that would be safe for a powerful AI to pursue. Its main proposal is QACI (question-answer counterfactual interval).

key_work.title: Orthogonal: A new agent foundations alignment organization
key_work.plain_summary: The launch post explaining why Orthogonal works on formal, mathematical approaches to aligning superintelligence.

key_work.title: Orthogonal's Formal-Goal Alignment theory of change
key_work.plain_summary: Argues the safest route is to give AI a precisely specified goal rather than hoping trained behaviour generalises well.

key_work.title: formalizing the QACI alignment formal-goal
key_work.plain_summary: A technical attempt to write the QACI goal — roughly 'do what a human would conclude after long reflection' — as mathematics.

key_work.title: How LDT helps reduce the AI arms race
key_work.plain_summary: Uses decision theory to argue that AI developers have reasons to cooperate rather than race.

key_work.title: Epistemic states as a potential benign prior
key_work.plain_summary: Explores a technical idea for giving an AI a safe starting assumption about the world.

status_raw: active (small); latest publication listed on its site is dated 31 Aug 2024

warnings.text: Approaches that rely on trained behaviour generalising well may fail for superintelligent systems.
Racing dynamics between AI developers increase the risk of catastrophe.

recommendations.text: Pursue formal-goal alignment: specify mathematically what a powerful AI should aim for.
AI developers should cooperate rather than race ('we're all in this together').
